title: Olesya
author: Alexander Kuprin
publication_note: first published in the newspaper «Киевлянин» (Kyiv), 1898, with the subtitle «From memories of Volhynia»; first separate edition 1905
source_note: Text from ru.wikisource.org, after A. I. Kuprin, Complete Works (St Petersburg: A. F. Marx, 1912), vol. 5.

art_alt.1_stove: A dark manor room in a blizzard: a forester squatting at an open stove with a bundle of firewood, a young gentleman standing by
art_alt.1b_village: A snowy Polesye village of low thatched huts, three peasants in sheepskins standing in the road with their caps off
art_alt.1c_patient: A table with bottles of medicine and two eggs, an old peasant woman standing by while the young gentleman looks on
art_alt.1d_lesson: A forester with a black beard bent over a table by a candle, slowly drawing letters with a pen
art_alt.2_empty_house: A big old manor house in a snowstorm, one lit window among dark ones, pines bent by the wind
art_alt.2b_stove_talk: A room by lamplight with a green shade, a bearded forester at the glowing stove and the master pacing
art_alt.2c_witch_driven: An old woman and a little girl driven out into the snowy forest by village lads with sticks, a broken hut behind them
art_alt.3_morning_guns: A thaw-morning room: a single-barrelled gun on the table and a forester cleaning it by the bright window
art_alt.3b_snow_forest: A pink winter morning in a pine forest, a hunter with a gun and a hare bounding across the snow
art_alt.3d_lost_marsh: A hunter wading through a snowy marsh among hummocks, a small hut far away between the trees
art_alt.3e_hut_ext: A hut on piles in a marsh, one side sunk so it looks lame, rags stuffed in its windows, snow on the thatch
art_alt.3f_hut_int: Inside the hut: an old woman on the floor stripping feathers, a huge stove, two starlings on the ledge, a stranger at the door
art_alt.3g_cards: An old woman laying worn cards in an eight-pointed star on a table, a hunter watching
art_alt.3h_olesya_enters: A tall girl in a red skirt flinging open the door, holding up her apron with three tiny finches
art_alt.3i_path_fence: A girl in a red skirt showing a hunter the path through the pines, a wattle fence beside them
art_alt.3j_red_skirt: A hunter on a hillock looking back: far off, the hut with a red spot on its porch against the snow
art_alt.4_spring_village: Early spring: brown streams in the village street, sparrows on the willows, white clouds in a blue sky
art_alt.4c_spinning: Olesya spinning flax on a high bench, her granny at the stove, the guest on a low stool
art_alt.4d_cards_olesya: Olesya with a red bead necklace sitting at the table with the cards, telling the guest his fortune
art_alt.4e_mill: A water mill by a dark pond under the moon, one lit window and the wheel turning
art_alt.4h_exile: A line of convicts in grey coats walking in chains along a snowy road, guarded by soldiers
art_alt.1e_pen: A big rough hand drawing a wobbly letter with a pen on paper under a candle
art_alt.3k_olesya_close: Olesya close up in the snow, proud and laughing, a red bead necklace at her throat
art_alt.8d_book: The constable pushing out a thick finger as he counts the points of a police book on the table
art_alt.4g_horror: Olesya's face with wide, fixed eyes, as if she saw something that is not there; red beads at her throat
art_alt.5_supper: Supper in the hut: a steaming pot on an embroidered cloth, granny eating greedily, Olesya serving
art_alt.5b_forest_road: A forest road at sunset with puddles and the first bluebells, a man and a girl in a red skirt walking
art_alt.5c_knife: A small knife and a thin red cut on a forearm, three drops of blood falling
art_alt.5d_fall: A man lying flat on the forest road, a girl laughing and clapping her hands behind him
art_alt.5e_medusa: Olesya's stare, huge and dark blue, like a Medusa's head, a man recoiling at the edge
art_alt.6_evening_path: Two figures walking slowly along the forest edge in the evening light, birches and pines
art_alt.6b_tall_house: A seven-storey city house beside a tall pine of the same height, Olesya and the guest looking up
art_alt.6c_church_far: A small village church with a green dome across the fields, Olesya and the guest standing apart
art_alt.6d_yarmola_gloom: A forester at the gate of the manor turning away with a dark look, his dog at his feet, the master watching
art_alt.7_dejected: The hut in gloom: granny rocking with her head in her hands, Olesya silent, the guest standing
art_alt.7b_notice: A huge constable in a grey greatcoat in the hut doorway holding up a paper, the old woman cowering
art_alt.8_rain_garden: A window onto a rainy garden of lilacs, a plan of a forest tract drawn on the table
art_alt.8b_cart: A long chocolate-coloured horse with a drooping lip drawing a wicker cart whose one shaft is a rope; the constable driving

art_alt.10_threshold: Olesya turning with a pale, radiant face as the guest stands in the doorway, granny shuffling aside

art_alt.10e_moon_face: Two faces close together in the moonlight, her red beads at her throat

art_alt.11d_pale_tree: Olesya, pale, leaning against a tree trunk while the man holds her hands

art_alt.11f_young_moon: A thin young moon over pines, Olesya with tears in her eyes holding the man's hands
art_alt.12_ride: A man on a grey mottled horse riding across a green meadow, a white church ahead

art_alt.12c_lyre: A blind lyre-player on a stool in the shade of a fence, villagers sitting around him
art_alt.12d_clerk: A young estate clerk in a loud checked jacket and red tie laughing, the master angry

art_alt.12f_running: Olesya running down the road in torn clothes, stones flying after her, the crowd far behind

art_alt.13b_bed: Olesya lying on the bed with her face to the wall, granny beside her, the man at the door
art_alt.13d_arm: A girl's arm with two dark bruises held in a man's hands

art_alt.13g_black_cloud: A black cloud over half the sky, the hut under it, granny pointing, the man listening

art_alt.14b_yarmola_bed: Morning sun streaming through shutter cracks, the bearded forester standing over the master's bed
art_alt.14c_empty_hut: The empty hut after a hasty departure: bed frame, rags and rubbish on the floor, the door wide open

episodes.title: The Witch of the Marsh
episodes.blurb: A bored young writer snowed in at a Polesye village, a forester who cannot learn to read, a rumour of a witch in the marsh, and a girl with three finches in her apron.

episodes.title: The Cards and the Charm
episodes.blurb: Spring comes. Olesya will not read the cards twice, shows him a charm on a forest road, and then the constable orders the two women out of the forest.

episodes.title: Moonlight in the Pine Forest
episodes.blurb: A gun for the constable, a fever, a night in the moonlit pines, and a June evening when Ivan Timofeyevich asks Olesya to be his wife.

episodes.title: Trinity Day
episodes.blurb: Olesya goes to church for him. What the village does to her, the tale of the hare and the wolf, a storm of hail, and a string of red beads.

glossary: Polesye
a vast region of forest and marsh in the north of Ukraine and the south of Belarus; in Kuprin's time part of the Russian Empire.
Volhynia
a province of the Russian Empire (now north-western Ukraine) in which the story is set.
verst
a Russian measure of distance, a little over a kilometre (about two thirds of a mile).
arshin
an old Russian measure of length, about 71 centimetres.
constable (uryadnik)
the lowest rank of rural police officer in the Russian Empire, in charge of a district.
zlot, kopeck
small coins: a zlot was fifteen kopecks, a kopeck a hundredth of a rouble.
krupnik
a thick pottage of groats (here buckwheat) with bacon, onion and potatoes.
Trinity Day
the feast of Pentecost, a great church holiday and a day of fairs and heavy drinking in the village.
lyre-player (lirnik)
a blind wandering singer who accompanied old ballads (dumas) on a hurdy-gurdy-like lyre.
Pochaev
a famous monastery in Volhynia, defended in the legend against the Turks.
tar
in Ukraine, to smear a girl's gate with tar was to brand her as dishonoured.
summary: A young writer posted to a Polesye village goes looking for a witch in the marsh and finds Olesya, a free, proud forest girl who reads the cards, loves the birds, and will not be told what to fear. Kuprin's most tender story of first love and the cruelty of a village.
site_description: Ivan Timofeyevich, a city writer stranded for the winter in a village in Polesye, hears of a witch who lives in the marsh and goes to see her. In the cabin on hen's legs he meets her granddaughter Olesya, who tells fortunes, charms blood and does not fear anything but her fate. A story of a spring and summer in the forest, of love, of what a village does to the one who is different, and of a string of red beads. Kuprin's novella of 1898, one of the best loved in Russian.

ru.description: Иван Тимофеевич, городской литератор, проводит зиму в глухой деревне на Полесье и идёт посмотреть на ведьму, которая живёт в болоте. В избушке на курьих ножках он встречает Олесю, гадалку и лесную девушку, которая ничего не боится, кроме своей судьбы. Повесть Куприна 1898 года о весне, любви и жестокости деревни.
